 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. In this story Aaron Ashby has been invaluable during the Milwaukee Brewers' postseason run. As of Tuesday, he has a place in the MLB record book to show for it.
 Ashby entered Tuesday's World Series Game 4 against the Tampa Bay Rays having thrown 15 2/3 scoreless innings this postseason. Those frames arrived across eight appearances against the Padres, Dodgers and Rays as Milwaukee advanced to and took a 3-0 lead in the World Series while losing just one postseason game.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ashby made it 18 straight scoreless frames across nine appearances before Game 4 was over.
 New record for Aaron Ashby
 Ashby entered in the bottom of the ninth inning of Game 4, with the game tied 2-2 and a chance to make history. He delivered by retiring seven straight batters.
 With the first out of the ninth, Ashby tied Andrew Miller for the most consecutive scoreless innings in a single postseason by a relief pitcher, with 16. With the second out — a groundout by Junior Caminero — Ashby claimed the record as his own. He finished the frame with a groundout of Liam Hicks to extend his streak to 16 2/3 innings and send the contest to extras.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ashby then pitched a perfect 10th inning to push his streak to 17 2/3 scoreless frames and keep Milwaukee's hopes of a World Series sweep alive. He got one more out in the 11th inning, making the record 18 straight scoreless frames, before manager Pat Murphy removed him from the game.
 In the top of the 12th, Cooper Pratt hit a solo home run to give the Brewers the lead. But the Rays rallied and walked it off in the bottom of the frame , earning a 4-3 victory and forcing Game 5 on Wednesday.
 Miller set his record in 2016 with Cleveland, earning ALCS MVP honors in the process. He didn't finish that postseason unblemished. He allowed three earned runs in four World Series appearances, including two in the Game 7 classic that the Chicago Cubs won in extra innings to secure their first and only World Series title since 1908.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Before Game 3, Miller said he wasn't concerned about losing the record, as he praised Ashby with Wisconsin's 620 WTMJ :
 "It's a blast to watch. I have no concern about him passing my record, I'm more enjoying his run. It's a really fun team to watch as a whole, but it's always fun seeing a middle reliever be the glue guy and help them win games. One of the best pitchers in the game, he's on top of it at the right time."
 Aaron Ashby has been critical for the Brewers during their postseason run and has now etched his name in the MLB record book.
 (AP Photo/Ashley Landis) Can Ashby extend his record?
 With at least one more game on tap, Ashby will look to avoid the same fate as Miller and continue his scoreless streak as one of the most valuable players in Milwaukee's pursuit of the franchise's first World Series championship.
 Per Sarah Langs, Ashby is the first pitcher in postseason history to record at least five outs in six consecutive appearances without allowing any runs. He has done it in seven.
 Ashby also has a chance to top Goose Gossage for the most innings in a single postseason by a reliever without allowing a run. Gossage pitched 14 1/3 scoreless postseason innings for the 1981 New York Yankees. The Yankees lost to the Dodgers 4-2 in that year's World Series.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ashby has already thrown more innings than Gossage, but he needs to finish his postseason scoreless to claim that record.
 As for the most scoreless innings in a single postseason by a pitcher of any kind, that record is almost certainly out of Ashby's reach. That mark belongs to Hall of Famer Christy Mathewson, who pitched three complete-game shutouts (or 27 scoreless innings) for the 1905 New York Giants on the way to a 4-1 World Series victory over the Philadelphia Athletics.
